With paired row matrices $A,B\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$, solve $\min_{\Omega^T\Omega=I}\|A-B\Omega\|_F^2$. Expanding gives constant terms minus $2\operatorname{tr}(\Omega^TB^TA)$. Let $B^TA=U\Sigma V^T$; maximizing that trace yields $\Omega=UV^T$. Thus a new row embedding $b$ maps to $b\Omega$. [1](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book2.html)

To see optimality, set $C=U^T\Omega V$, which is orthogonal. The trace is $\sum_i\sigma_i C_{ii}\leq\sum_i\sigma_i$, achieved at $C=I$. Reflections are allowed; requiring determinant +1 needs a sign correction on the smallest singular direction. Center paired data if translation matters, and apply the corresponding means during inference. The solution preserves distances under its map but cannot repair arbitrary semantic changes between encoders.
